attributes.FilterMethod: On the filtered VCF: GATK CNNScoreVariants scores each call, then FilterVariantTranches filters on those scores with SNP and INDEL sensitivity tranches (sarek output docs). On the unfiltered haplotypecaller.vcf.gz, used only when that filtering did not run: none
None named in the sarek output docs: DeepVariant's VCF as the caller wrote it
On the filtered VCF: a filter the sarek output docs do not describe (they list only the unfiltered VCF). On the unfiltered freebayes.vcf.gz, used only when no filtered VCF exists: none
None named in the sarek output docs: all potential variant loci, including non-variant loci with a non-trivial level of variant evidence
None named in the sarek output docs: SVs and indels scored and genotyped under a diploid model for the sample

MappedPercent.note: samtools flagstat on the recalibrated alignment (sarek's <sample>.recal row)

MismatchPercent.note: samtools' mismatches per mapped base on the recalibrated alignment (sarek's <sample>.recal row); MultiQC writes it as a percentage, as rnaseq's samtools_stats-error_rate

deliberately_unmapped.why: Secondary and supplementary BAM records, in millions: a record count, not a share, and D.SEQ has no attribute for it.
In millions, and it counts mapped BAM records (each mate of a pair), not reads. MappedPercent already records the mapped share from the same samtools run.
Sits near 100 on BWA's paired-end alignments and is absent for single-end data, so it tells samples apart by nothing.

Reads with mapping quality 0, which BWA gives a read placed equally well elsewhere: as much a property of the reference's repeats as of the library, and not the STAR multimapped share MultimappedPercent holds.
In millions, and it counts BAM records (both mates of a pair), not reads, so it is no stand-in for TotalReads.
Mean insert size of the aligned pairs. D.SEQ has no insert-size attribute; one would be a schema request, not a mapping.
Share of bases covered at 1x or more: near 100 on any usable alignment, so it separates nothing. A.ALN keeps the 10x and 30x shares.
Share of bases covered at 5x or more: between the 1x and 10x marks, it adds little beside them. A.ALN keeps the 10x and 30x shares.
Share of bases covered at 50x or more. A.ALN keeps the 10x and 30x shares and the median coverage, which already shows a deep run; a 50x field would be a schema request.

unmapped_files.why: sarek's restart samplesheets (markduplicates, recalibrated, variantcalled): inputs for a later sarek step, not results.
Indexes, dictionaries and intervals sarek built from the reference (with --save_reference): reference files, not sample data.
Per-tool QC reports, per sample (FastQC, fastp, mosdepth, samtools, MarkDuplicates, bcftools, VCFtools, snpEff, VEP) or per run (NGSCheckMate); their numbers are read through MultiQC.
GATK BaseRecalibrator tables: the model ApplyBQSR used to make the registered recalibrated CRAM, an intermediate of that file.
Manta's unscored candidate SVs and small indels, the input to its own scoring and to Strelka; the scored diploid_sv VCF is registered.
snpEff and VEP annotated copies of the registered caller VCFs; annotation is off in Luria launches, and a copy is not a second call set.

Somatic tumor/normal pair outputs, anything under a <tumor>_vs_<normal> folder at any depth: a pair's row needs two parents, which no rule can express yet, so they wait for a pair-level rule. A germline sample whose name contains "_vs_" is ruled out too, since its folder matches.
